title: Transactional email service with templates and provider abstraction
goal: Provide a transactional email service with a provider abstraction (Postmark first), typed templates and safe rendering, so other lanes can send invite and account emails without knowing the provider.
scope_in: `EmailService.send(templateId, to, params, opts)` that renders HTML + text, validates inputs and hands a `RenderedEmail` to an `EmailProvider`.
Providers: `PostmarkProvider` (HTTPS via global `fetch`, no SDK), `MemoryEmailProvider` (tests/dev capture), `ConsoleEmailProvider` (local dev, logs template name only).
Template registry with typed params for `workspace_invite`, `account_deletion_scheduled`, `export_ready`; plain-text part mandatory.
Per-recipient send limit via the B009 rate-limit primitives; BullMQ job `email-send` for asynchronous delivery with retries.
scope_out: Invite business logic (B029), magic-link login emails (B014), notification digests (B063).
Inbound bounce/complaint webhooks and a suppression list (future lane).
build_against: `MemoryEmailProvider` and a local HTTP stub standing in for the Postmark API (started in tests); B009 in-memory rate limiter; nothing external.
interfaces: TS: `interface EmailProvider { name: string; send(msg: RenderedEmail, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<{ providerMessageId: string }> }`
TS: `interface RenderedEmail { to: string; from: string; subject: string; html: string; text: string; tag: string }`

TS: `interface EmailService { send<T extends TemplateId>(id: T, to: string, params: TemplateParams[T], opts?: { idempotencyKey?: string }): Promise<{ queued: true; jobId: string }>; render<T extends TemplateId>(id: T, params: TemplateParams[T], locale?: string): RenderedEmail }`
TS: `type TemplateId = 'workspace_invite' | 'account_deletion_scheduled' | 'export_ready'` with a `registerTemplate` extension point for later lanes.
BullMQ queue `email-send` (attempts 5, backoff exponential 30 s base with jitter).
acceptance: Rendering `workspace_invite` with `inviterName` `<script>x</script>` yields HTML where the string is escaped (`<script>`) and the text part contains the raw characters without markup.
Any `to`, `subject` or name containing CR or LF is rejected with a validation error before reaching the provider (header injection).
`to` is lower-cased and rejected when > 254 chars or not a valid address; subject is <= 150 chars.
The 6th email of the same template to the same address inside one hour is rejected with 429-class error carrying `retry_after_s`.
A provider timeout after 10 s aborts the request and the job is retried up to 5 times; the 5th failure moves the job to the dead-letter set and increments `email_failed_total`.
Sending twice with the same `idempotencyKey` within 24 h results in exactly one provider call.
Logs for a send contain template id, job id and provider message id, and do not contain the recipient address, params or URLs (log-capture test).
With `EMAIL_PROVIDER=memory` the sent message is retrievable from `MemoryEmailProvider.sent` for test assertions.
tests: email.render.test.ts: golden HTML/text for each template, escaping property test with random strings.
email.postmark.test.ts: against the HTTP stub (200, 422 permanent error, 500, timeout).
email.logging.test.ts: no recipient or URL in logs.
guardrails: Template params MUST be HTML-escaped by the renderer; callers MUST NOT pass pre-built HTML.
MUST NOT log recipient addresses, tokens, URLs from params or the email body.
Links that contain secrets (invite tokens) MUST be built by the caller and passed as one `url` param; the renderer MUST NOT add tracking parameters or redirectors.
Permanent provider rejections (4xx other than 429) MUST NOT be retried.
The Postmark token MUST come from the secrets loader and MUST NOT appear in error messages.
failure_modes: Provider 429/5xx -> retry with backoff and jitter, honour `Retry-After`.
Provider 4xx permanent (invalid recipient) -> job fails without retry, metric `email_rejected_total`.
Redis unavailable at enqueue -> `send` throws a retryable 503-class error; no email is sent inline as a fallback.
Unknown template id at runtime -> throws at enqueue time, never at delivery.
notes: Only three templates are in this lane; other lanes add theirs through `registerTemplate` in their own files. Email copy is server-side here, unlike notifications (CT-NOTIF-PAYLOAD uses keys); this is intentional because email has no client message table. CONTRACT GAP: none for the contracts consumed.
